name: Schneider National, Inc.
domainRelevance: Schneider National is a top-three North American transportation and logistics provider, operating ~13,000 tractors and 35,000+ trailers across trucking, intermodal, and logistics segments. The company is a critical node in supply-chain execution for CPG, automotive, and retail distribution, with particular strength in dedicated contract carriage and port-terminal operations. Diesel fuel exposure, driver-wage inflation, and freight-rate cyclicality are core operational levers.
portalRelevance: Schneider National serves as a demand-sensing and capacity-constraint signal for the broader supply chain. Its quarterly operating ratio, fleet utilization, and freight-rate realizations are leading indicators of manufacturing and retail health; its intermodal volumes and port-terminal throughput directly reflect import/export cycles. As a peer to J.B. Hunt and Knight-Swift, SNDR's margin trajectory and capital allocation reveal shipper pricing power and modal-shift dynamics critical to inventory-in-transit costs.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly freight-rate indices (spot and contract) via DAT and Coyote platforms; disclosed in quarterly earnings calls
Quarterly operating ratio and fuel surcharge realization; disclosed in 10-K Item 7 MD&A
Intermodal volume and port-terminal throughput; disclosed in segment reporting (10-K Item 8)
Driver turnover and wage-inflation metrics; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors and compensation disclosures

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Freight-rate environment classification (spot weakness vs. contract strength) via quarterly earnings guidance
Fleet utilization and tractor-to-trailer ratio; disclosed in quarterly investor presentations
Intermodal modal-shift trajectory vs. trucking; inferred from segment margin trends in 10-K
Debt-to-EBITDA and covenant headroom; disclosed in 10-K Item 8 debt schedules and 8-K refinancing events

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern-match: operating-ratio compression vs. prior-year same-quarter; signals shipper pricing power erosion or fuel-cost pass-through failure
Intermodal margin divergence from trucking; indicates modal-shift inflection or port-congestion relief
Driver turnover spike above 80% annualized; signals wage-inflation spiral or capacity constraint ahead
Debt refinancing at rising spreads; indicates credit-market repricing of freight-cycle risk

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedge diesel exposure via NYMEX crude and heating-oil futures; target 40–60% of forward 12-month volume
Monitor FMCSA hours-of-service rule changes and ELD mandate compliance; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A
Track EPA Tier 4 emission standards and capital-expenditure impact; disclosed in 10-K Item 7 capex guidance
Maintain debt covenant cushion >1.5x; disclosed in 10-K Item 8 debt covenants and quarterly 10-Q filings

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Long SNDR if operating ratio inflects below 95% and intermodal volumes accelerate; short if ratio exceeds 98% and driver turnover >85%
Reduce position if debt refinancing spreads widen >150 bps above investment-grade median
Increase exposure if management guides to pricing power recovery in next quarter's earnings call
Monitor 8-K filings for major customer wins (dedicated contract carriage) or losses; disclosed in Item 8.01 events

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Validate signal via Q+1 earnings print: operating ratio, fuel surcharge realization, intermodal volume growth
Track share-price reaction to freight-rate index prints and competitor earnings (J.B. Hunt, Knight-Swift)
Monitor 10-Q filings for covenant compliance and debt-level changes; quarterly disclosure in Item 1A
Assess driver-wage inflation vs. fuel-surcharge pass-through; disclosed in quarterly earnings call guidance

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Reweight diesel-exposure sensitivity if EV adoption accelerates; monitor capex guidance for electric-tractor pilots
Recalibrate intermodal-margin model if port-automation reduces terminal labor costs; disclosed in investor presentations
Update driver-wage inflation elasticity if labor-market tightness persists; adjust wage-cost forecasts in 10-K Item 1A
Refine debt-covenant headroom model if credit spreads persist at elevated levels; monitor quarterly 10-Q debt schedules

functionalNetwork.model: Schneider National operates as a distributed logistics brain: its trucking fleet and intermodal terminals function as sensory-motor nodes capturing real-time freight demand and port-congestion signals; its dedicated contract-carriage business (DMN role) anchors shipper relationships and pricing power; its fuel-hedging and driver-wage management (PFC/limbic) regulate operational margin; and its debt and capital-allocation decisions (OFC) integrate market-cycle signals into fleet-expansion and shareholder-return policies. The company's quarterly earnings and 8-K filings emit leading indicators of supply-chain health that downstream retailers and manufacturers depend on for inventory-in-transit cost modeling.
